Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays show peripheral, non-segmental opacities that are more prominent in the lower lung zones, a pattern classically associated with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) in patients with asthma and nasal polyposis. This "photographic negative of pulmonary edema" appearance helps distinguish it from other conditions like sarcoidosis (central/perilymphatic) or TB (apical).
